sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2: Algebraically prove PSI symmetry between P and Q, and calculate PSI for two-bin distributions P equal to [0.5, 0.5] and Q equal to [0.8, 0.2] against the 0.25 quarantine threshold. Select Option A, B, or C above me!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Checkpoint 2! Remember that log of p over q is negative log of q over p, flipping the difference cleanly! Sum Bin 1 at 0.14100 plus Bin 2 at 0.27489 and choose Option A, B, or C above me!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely verified! Swapping P and Q negates both the weight difference and the natural logarithm, cancelling identically so PSI is strictly symmetric. For the two-bin shift, 0.14100 plus 0.27489 equals 0.4159, exceeding 0.25 and triggering immediate batch quarantine!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Incorrect! Standard KL divergence is asymmetric, whereas PSI equals D_KL of Q to P plus D_KL of P to Q, making it symmetric. Computing both bins gives 0.3 times log 1.6 plus negative 0.3 times log 0.4 equals 0.4159—severe shift requiring quarantine!
